title: Imperatle empire
description: One empire of the game. The file name must be <slug>.json.

slug.description: Stable id: lowercase words separated by hyphens, e.g. "mongol-empire". Never change it after launch (players' history points to it).

name.description: Name shown in the guess list and in the answer.

peak.description: Year of the greatest territorial extent, the moment the map shows. The era clue is computed from it.

end.description: When the empire ended, or null if it still exists (its duration then runs to the current year).

durationNotes.description: Optional caveat shown next to the duration, e.g. which phase of a longer state the dates cover.

religionNotes.description: Optional caveat shown next to the religion, e.g. that most subjects followed other faiths.

area.description: Largest area ever controlled (same moment as peak).

mapAccuracy.description: How well historians know the borders on the map: Precise (High), Approximate (Medium), Speculative (Low).

continents.description: Every continent where the empire held territory at its peak.

primaryContinents.description: Where most of the territory was: one continent, or two when it was split about evenly between them. Must be among continents.

language.description: Main language of the government and the elite.

religion.description: Official religion, or that of the ruling elite.

curiosities.description: Exactly 3, from the least obvious to the most obvious. They're revealed in this order.

details.description: Optional longer explanation of the clue, shown only once the round is over (it may name what the clue hides).

aliases.description: Other names the guess list also matches, never shown as the answer: spellings ("Mughal", "Mugal"), other languages, or the country an empire is often called by ("China" for every Chinese dynasty).

summary.description: What the empire was, in a few sentences, shown once the round is over.

wikipedia.description: Wikipedia article links, shown once the round is over (never before, they'd give the answer away).

map.description: Optional while the map isn't ready (the game shows a placeholder). The shape is built by apps/web/scripts/maps/build-shapes.mjs into Content/shapes/<slug>.json.

parts.description: Merged into the shape: Cliopatria polities, each at a year its record covers (usually the peak year), plus today's territories for land the dataset misses and areas drawn by hand in the empire generator (added, or cut out of everything else). At least one polity.

polity.description: Cliopatria "Name", exactly, e.g. "Mongol Empire" or "(British Empire)".

year.description: Negative = BCE. There is no year 0.

country.description: A territory as it is today, for land Cliopatria misses: Natural Earth's 3-letter code (ADM0_A3), e.g. "PYF" for French Polynesia.

box.description: Optional: only the part of the territory inside [west, south, east, north], in degrees, e.g. [-180, 60, -165, 70.5] for the tip of Chukotka.

draw.description: "add" merges the area into the shape; "remove" cuts it out of everything else.

ring.description: The area's outline, traced in the empire generator: [longitude, latitude] points in degrees. Longitudes run on past ±180 for a ring drawn across the antimeridian.

year.description: Negative = BCE, as historians write it: -27 is 27 BCE. There is no year 0.

precision.description: Exact, Approximate (circa) or Century (only the century is known).
